source_observations.observation: Five qualifying compound finals and five distinct bearers. Long ī in the body-wide heat example.
The compound-final a of 5.4.74 lies inside the recognized pathin history. This displayed Kāśikā has a short i in the heat example.

source_observations.locator: Bhaṭṭikāvya 5.100–101, Ambuda with the numbered parallel
source_observations.observation: The bird is the actor. The two wings are possessors in the dual. Their spread is the object of the participle.

source_observations.locator: Jayamaṅgalā ad Bhaṭṭi 5.101, Bāpata edition, Bombay, Nirṇaya-Sāgara, 1887, search the verse beginning dhunvan
source_observations.observation: Explains dhunvan as shaking, relates the wings to vitānam and explicitly applies the coverage rule and kha to the adjective.

source_observations.locator: Apte, vitāna, substantive senses of extension and canopy
source_observations.observation: Masculine and neuter are recorded for the spreading or canopy. The accusative singular alone leaves gender ambiguous.
The unworn cloth can have the requisite length. Nyāsa distinguishes endpoint contact from complete coverage.
Three ordered pairs, with distinct patient, object and destination roles. The board has opposite directions of travel.
Separate Haima rules for shoe, board and food. Treat its extra yathākāma input as local to that grammar.
Bālā assigns u to the initial of avara. Tattva also reports o on para and retention of that vowel. Kāśikā distinguishes independent paramparā.
Each adviser has advisers in turn. The next sentence puts the chain in the nominative with singular bhinatti.
The second paragraph has comparative parovarīyān and parovarīyāṃsam modifying the chant. Its longer stem is visible directly.
Future gāmin preserves the object accusative at 2.3.70. Both isolated shores and the reversal are explicitly added.
